front.title: Theology of The Urantia Book
front.sub: From God to the Eternal Ascent: Thirty-Seven Doctrines in the Words of the Revelation
front.author: Jay Han
front.preface1: The Urantia Book is a vast revelation of more than two thousand pages. It answers nearly every theological question humanity has asked: about God and the universe, celestial beings and mankind, sin and salvation, the life of Jesus and the eternal ascent. Yet its answers are scattered across the book, and grasping a single doctrine in full means moving back and forth among many papers.
front.preface2: This book gathers those scattered teachings into thirty-seven topics. Each chapter first states the gist of its subject, then sets out its key propositions one by one, adding to each a short explanation followed by the passages of The Urantia Book that support it. The explanations are only a guide; the heart of every chapter is the quoted text itself, so quotation and commentary stand roughly in a ratio of six to four.
front.preface3: The quotations in this English edition are reproduced word for word from the original English text, each followed by its paper:section.paragraph reference. The explanations carry no references, so that readers can easily tell the revelation from the commentary and can always turn to the source to read a passage in its full context.
front.preface4: The eight parts follow the classic order of theology: beginning with God, moving through the universe and its beings, man, sin and salvation, Jesus and the kingdom of heaven, and the religious life, and ending with the eternal ascent. The book may be read straight through or topic by topic. The questions at the end of each chapter are offered for personal reflection and for study groups.
front.preface5: The theology of The Urantia Book is not knowledge for the head alone. May this book serve as a small stepping-stone from knowledge about God to the experience of knowing God.
ch01.sub: The Reality and Personality of God
ch01.sum: Urantia theology begins with the Universal Father. He is the First Source and Center of all things and beings, the creator, controller, and infinite upholder of all creation. The universe was made for beings who can know God and return his love, and every such being stands before the call, "Be you perfect, even as I am perfect." This chapter considers in turn the name of God, his reality, his spirit nature and mystery, and his personality. God is not an object to be proved by logic but a reality met in experience; he is infinite, and yet a person who can befriend us.
ch01.s1: Source and Goal of All Things
ch01.s1.u1.k: God is creator, controller, and infinite upholder.
ch01.s1.u1.p: Urantia Book theology starts from the order of these three words. First the One who brought all things into being, then the One who governs them in order, and last the One who upholds them without end. Notice too the observation that only when mankind grasped the idea of one God in place of many gods could creation and control be understood as belonging to a single Person. In polytheism the world is a battleground of rival powers; under the one God the universe becomes a household governed by a single will.

text: First think of God as a creator, then as a controller, and lastly as an infinite upholder. … Only the concept of the Universal Father—one God in the place of many gods—enabled mortal man to comprehend the Father as divine creator and infinite controller.

ch01.s1.u2.k: The universe was made to be inhabited by beings who know and love God.
ch01.s1.u2.p: Creation has a purpose. Stars and planets are not ends in themselves; they are homes for beings who can receive the divine affection and love God in return. Seen this way, the universe is not a vast machine but a stage for relationship. Before man ever sought God, God made the world in order to meet man.

text: The myriads of planetary systems were all made to be eventually inhabited by many different types of intelligent creatures, beings who could know God, receive the divine affection, and love him in return. … "God created the heavens and formed the earth; he established the universe and created this world not in vain; he formed it to be inhabited."

ch01.s1.u3.k: The call to be perfect as God is perfect is the first duty and the certain destiny of every creature.
ch01.s1.u3.p: The command to be perfect is not a burden that holds out an unreachable ideal. The text calls it the final and certain destiny of man's eternal spiritual progress. The one desire of God-knowing creatures is not to become infinite but to become like him, as they are in their own spheres. The command is at the same time a promise.

text: God-knowing creatures have only one supreme ambition, just one consuming desire, and that is to become, as they are in their spheres, like him as he is in his Paradise perfection of personality and in his universal sphere of righteous supremacy. From the Universal Father who inhabits eternity there has gone forth the supreme mandate, "Be you perfect, even as I am perfect."

This magnificent and universal injunction to strive for the attainment of the perfection of divinity is the first duty, and should be the highest ambition, of all the struggling creature creation of the God of perfection. This possibility of the attainment of divine perfection is the final and certain destiny of all man's eternal spiritual progress.

ch01.s2.u1.k: God reveals himself not by name but by nature.
ch01.s2.u1.p: The statement that God has never revealed himself by name carries deep theological weight. He reveals himself only by nature, not by name. Even the name Father is a confession of relationship before it is a title handed down from above. When we believe ourselves to be his children, we naturally come to call him Father.

text: The First Source and Universe Center has never revealed himself by name, only by nature. If we believe that we are the children of this Creator, it is only natural that we should eventually call him Father. But this is the name of our own choosing, and it grows out of the recognition of our personal relationship with the First Source and Center.

Those who know God through the revelations of the bestowals of the Paradise Sons, eventually yield to the sentimental appeal of the touching relationship of the creature-Creator association and refer to God as "our Father."

ch01.s2.u2.k: More important than any name is to know him and to aspire to be like him.
ch01.s2.u2.p: The history of religion is crowded with quarrels over the name of God, yet the text places little weight on the name itself. What matters is knowing him and becoming like him. When we meet neighbors who call on God by another name, this sentence gives us ground for humility and generosity.

text: The name he is given is of little importance; the significant thing is that you should know him and aspire to be like him.

ch01.s2.u3.k: God never compels worship; he receives the voluntary dedication of the will as the choicest gift.
ch01.s2.u3.p: That the Almighty never coerces tells us much about his character, for love cannot be had by force. Man's choicest gift to God is the affectionate dedication of his will to doing the Father's will. This freely given consecration is the only gift of true value.

text: The Universal Father never imposes any form of arbitrary recognition, formal worship, or slavish service upon the intelligent will creatures of the universes. … The affectionate dedication of the human will to the doing of the Father's will is man's choicest gift to God; in fact, such a consecration of creature will constitutes man's only possible gift of true value to the Paradise Father.

ch01.s3.u1.k: God is primal reality in the spirit world, neither manlike nor machinelike.
ch01.s3.u1.p: This passage places God in three realms at once: primal reality in the spirit world, the source of truth in the mind spheres, the One who overshadows all in the material realms. The phrase "neither manlike nor machinelike" rules out both the picture of God as an enlarged human being and the picture of God as impersonal law.

text: God is primal reality in the spirit world; God is the source of truth in the mind spheres; God overshadows all throughout the material realms. … God is neither manlike nor machinelike.

ch01.s3.u2.k: God is not another name for human ideals or natural law; he is more.
ch01.s3.u2.p: Since the modern era many thinkers have explained God as reality idealized or a nickname for nature. The text grants that such ideas may hold partly true in the minds of men, yet insists that God is more. And it fills that "more" not with an abstract concept but with a saving person and a loving Father.

text: The eternal God is infinitely more than reality idealized or the universe personalized. … The Universal Father is not a synonym for nature, neither is he natural law personified. … God may be any or all of these concepts in the minds of men, but he is more. He is a saving person and a loving Father to all who enjoy spiritual peace on earth, and who crave to experience personality survival in death.

ch01.s3.u3.k: The existence of God is not proved by logic; it is realized in experience.
ch01.s3.u3.p: This passage draws a clear line through the long debate over proofs of God. God is not the object of experiment or deduction. That does not make faith irrational: the true concept of God is reasonable to logic, plausible to philosophy, and essential to religion. But the final confirmation is entrusted to the experience of each person who knows God.

text: The existence of God can never be proved by scientific experiment or by the pure reason of logical deduction. God can be realized only in the realms of human experience; nevertheless, the true concept of the reality of God is reasonable to logic, plausible to philosophy, essential to religion, and indispensable to any hope of personality survival.

Those who know God have experienced the fact of his presence; such God-knowing mortals hold in their personal experience the only positive proof of the existence of the living God which one human being can offer to another.

ch01.s3.u4.k: The indwelling divine presence is disclosed in God-consciousness, God-seeking, and the craving to be like God.
ch01.s3.u4.p: It is a distinctive teaching of this revelation that the evidence for God lies not outside man but within him. The capacity to know God, the urge to find him, and the craving to be like him are all ways in which the presence of the Thought Adjuster becomes known. The very heart that seeks God is already a sign that God is near.

text: The actuality of the existence of God is demonstrated in human experience by the indwelling of the divine presence, the spirit Monitor sent from Paradise to live in the mortal mind of man and there to assist in evolving the immortal soul of eternal survival. The presence of this divine Adjuster in the human mind is disclosed by three experiential phenomena:
1. The intellectual capacity for knowing God—God-consciousness.
2. The spiritual urge to find God—God-seeking.
3. The personality craving to be like God—the wholehearted desire to do the Father's will.

ch01.s4: God as Spirit and as Mystery
ch01.s4.u1.k: God is spirit; he is not like us in form and physique.
ch01.s4.u1.p: Read literally, the phrase "in his image" leads us to imagine God in human shape. The text instead interprets that image not as a body but as the Mystery Monitor that indwells man. Being invisible does not mean being unreal.

text: "God is spirit." … Even though you are "the offspring of God," you ought not to think that the Father is like yourselves in form and physique because you are said to be created "in his image"—indwelt by Mystery Monitors dispatched from the central abode of his eternal presence. Spirit beings are real, notwithstanding they are invisible to human eyes; even though they have not flesh and blood.

ch01.s4.u2.k: Though the eyes of the flesh cannot see God, the spiritualized mind discerns him by faith.
ch01.s4.u2.p: God is invisible not because he hides but because his glory is greater than any material being could endure. Yet the text immediately opens another way: in place of the eyes of the flesh there is the vision of faith. Unlike the worldly rule that seeing is believing, in the spirit world believing is the way of seeing.

text: The Universal Father is not invisible because he is hiding himself away from the lowly creatures of materialistic handicaps and limited spiritual endowments. … The glory and the spiritual brilliance of the divine personality presence is impossible of approach by the lower groups of spirit beings or by any order of material personalities. … But it is not necessary to see God with the eyes of the flesh in order to discern him by the faith-vision of the spiritualized mind.

ch01.s4.u3.k: The greatest mystery of God is his indwelling of the human mind.
ch01.s4.u3.p: The mystery arises not because God is far away but because he is so near. That the Infinite dwells within a finite mind is beyond the reach of philosophy. Yet the text adds that, to one who experiences him, God is not a mystery but a reality. He may be hard to explain, but he can be met.

text: The infinity of the perfection of God is such that it eternally constitutes him mystery. And the greatest of all the unfathomable mysteries of God is the phenomenon of the divine indwelling of mortal minds. The manner in which the Universal Father sojourns with the creatures of time is the most profound of all universe mysteries; the divine presence in the mind of man is the mystery of mysteries.

As a reality in human spiritual experience God is not a mystery. But when an attempt is made to make plain the realities of the spirit world to the physical minds of the material order, mystery appears: mysteries so subtle and so profound that only the faith-grasp of the God-knowing mortal can achieve the philosophic miracle of the recognition of the Infinite by the finite, the discernment of the eternal God by the evolving mortals of the material worlds of time and space.

ch01.s5.u1.k: Do not let the infinity of God obscure his personality.
ch01.s5.u1.p: The greater we conceive God to be, the more easily we picture him as an impersonal force or principle. The text warns squarely against this danger. As the question asks, "He who planned the ear, shall he not hear?" The One who made personality cannot be less than personal. God is infinite, and he is a person.

text: Do not permit the magnitude of God, his infinity, either to obscure or eclipse his personality. "He who planned the ear, shall he not hear? He who formed the eye, shall he not see?" … God is both infinite and personal; he is an infinite personality.
Without God and except for his great and central person, there would be no personality throughout all the vast universe of universes. God is personality.

ch01.s5.u2.k: God can know and be known, love and be loved, and befriend us.
ch01.s5.u2.p: The doctrine that God is a person is not an abstract debate; it concerns the possibility of relationship. Between nonpersonal things there can be interaction but never fellowship. Because God is a person, man can commune with him, trust him, and be known as the friend of God. Goodness and love have meaning only between persons.

text: Notwithstanding that God is an eternal power, a majestic presence, a transcendent ideal, and a glorious spirit, though he is all these and infinitely more, nonetheless, he is truly and everlastingly a perfect Creator personality, a person who can "know and be known," who can "love and be loved," and one who can befriend us; while you can be known, as other humans have been known, as the friend of God.

The concept of truth might possibly be entertained apart from personality, the concept of beauty may exist without personality, but the concept of divine goodness is understandable only in relation to personality. Only a person can love and be loved.

ch01.s5.u3.k: God is to science a cause, to philosophy an idea, to religion the loving heavenly Father.
ch01.s5.u3.p: Science, philosophy, and religion speak of the same God in different languages. This passage does not set them against one another but arranges them as levels. Science seeks a cause and philosophy a hypothesis of unity, while religion meets the personal Father in living experience. All three roads lead, in the end, to the same One.

text: God is to science a cause, to philosophy an idea, to religion a person, even the loving heavenly Father. God is to the scientist a primal force, to the philosopher a hypothesis of unity, to the religionist a living spiritual experience.

ch01.qs1: What might it mean for my faith to think of God first as creator, then as controller, and lastly as upholder?
ch01.qs2: How does the fact that God never compels worship change my relationship with him?
ch01.qs3: Have I known a moment when I experienced God as a person who can be known?
ch02.t: The Eternal Son and the Infinite Spirit
ch02.sub: God the Word and the God of Action
ch02.sum: The Universal Father is not alone. The Eternal Son is the perfect expression of the Father's first thought, and the Infinite Spirit is the united thought and word of Father and Son made manifest in action. The Son is the Word of God and the mercy of God, and by spirit gravity he draws all spiritual reality toward Paradise. The Infinite Spirit is the God of Action and the source of mind, who carries the Father's love and the Son's mercy to every creature as ministry. This chapter considers the nature and ministry of the Second and Third Sources and Centers, and asks how that ministry reaches human prayer, human mind, and the long ascent.
ch02.s1: The Eternal Son, the Word of the Father
ch02.s1.u1.k: The Eternal Son is the Second Source and Center, the personal revelation of the Father's spirit.
ch02.s1.u1.p: If the Father is infinite will, the Eternal Son is that will expressed as person; hence the Son is called the Personality Absolute alongside the Volitional Absolute. As the Father is first creator and then controller, the Son is first cocreator and then spiritual administrator. The Eternal Son is not a rival second God beside the Father but the personal revelation of the Father's own spirit.

text: The Eternal Son is the original and only-begotten Son of God. He is God the Son, the Second Person of Deity and the associate creator of all things. As the Father is the First Great Source and Center, so the Eternal Son is the Second Great Source and Center.

The Universal Father is first a creator and then a controller; the Eternal Son is first a cocreator and then a spiritual administrator. "God is spirit," and the Son is a personal revelation of that spirit. The First Source and Center is the Volitional Absolute; the Second Source and Center is the Personality Absolute.

ch02.s1.u2.k: He who has seen the Son has seen the Father, and the Father comes to us as a person through the Sons.
ch02.s1.u2.p: Because the Eternal Son is wholly like the Father, to know the Son is to know the Father. This truth applies not only to the Eternal Son but also to the Creator Sons who come to the local universes. Man receives personality directly from the Father as a gift, yet the way up to the Father is the living way the Sons have walked and shown.

text: The Eternal Son is the eternal Word of God. He is wholly like the Father; in fact, the Eternal Son is God the Father personally manifest to the universe of universes. And thus it was and is and forever will be true of the Eternal Son and of all the co-ordinate Creator Sons: "He who has seen the Son has seen the Father."

The Father comes down to you as a personality only through the divine Sons of the Eternal Son. And you attain the Father by this same living way; you ascend to the Father by the guidance of this group of divine Sons. And this remains true notwithstanding that your very personality is a direct bestowal of the Universal Father.

ch02.s1.u3.k: As God is love, the Son is mercy, and mercy is the Father's love in action.
ch02.s1.u3.p: The Son's mercy is nothing other than the Father's love. The Son does not persuade a stern Father to grant mercy; rather, the Father's love flows out in the Son as concrete care. The text likens the difference to a father's love and a mother's affection: the same love appears in the Father as a father's love and in the Son as something closer to a mother's affection.

text: God is love, the Son is mercy. Mercy is applied love, the Father's love in action in the person of his Eternal Son. … As love is comprehended on a sex planet, the love of God is more comparable to the love of a father, while the love of the Eternal Son is more like the affection of a mother.

ch02.s2: Spirit Gravity and the Way of Ascent
ch02.s2.u1.k: The spirit gravity of the Eternal Son literally pulls the soul of man Paradiseward.
ch02.s2.u1.p: As matter is held by the gravity of the Isle of Paradise, so true spiritual values are held by the spirit gravity of the Eternal Son. This pull is the very secret of the Paradise ascension of surviving human souls. Ascension is not only man's solitary climb; it is a response to a drawing power exerted unceasingly from God's side.

text: The spiritual-gravity pull of the Eternal Son constitutes the inherent secret of the Paradise ascension of surviving human souls. All genuine spirit values and all bona fide spiritualized individuals are held within the unfailing grasp of the spiritual gravity of the Eternal Son. … The spirit-gravity circuit literally pulls the soul of man Paradiseward.

ch02.s2.u2.k: Prayer that carries true spiritual value passes at once to Deity over the spirit-gravity circuit.
ch02.s2.u2.p: The spirit-gravity circuit is also the channel of prayer. Yet it responds not to the quantity or form of words but to the spiritual value of their content. A spiritual petition from a sincere heart reaches every divine personality concerned at once, while purely selfish and material requests find no lodgment in that circuit. The power of prayer lies in its motive.

text: The spirit-gravity circuit is the basic channel for transmitting the genuine prayers of the believing human heart from the level of human consciousness to the actual consciousness of Deity. That which represents true spiritual value in your petitions will be seized by the universal circuit of spirit gravity and will pass immediately and simultaneously to all divine personalities concerned.

The content of any petition which is not "spirit indited" can find no place in the universal spiritual circuit; such purely selfish and material requests fall dead; they do not ascend in the circuits of true spirit values. Such words are as "sounding brass and a tinkling cymbal."

ch02.s2.u3.k: The infinite Eternal Son is approachable through the Paradise Sons and the ministry of the Infinite Spirit.
ch02.s2.u3.p: The distance between the Infinite and finite man cannot be crossed by man's own strength, so the Deities have built a bridge. The Sons come down in bestowal, and the children of the Spirit stay near in patient ministry. Without this bestowal and ministry, beings of material origin could hardly hope to attain the Eternal Son.

text: The Eternal Son is infinite, but he is approachable through the persons of his Paradise Sons and through the patient ministry of the Infinite Spirit. Without the bestowal service of the Paradise Sons and the loving ministry of the creatures of the Infinite Spirit, beings of material origin could hardly hope to attain the Eternal Son.

The Eternal Son is the only avenue of approach to the Universal Father, and the Infinite Spirit is the only means of attaining the Eternal Son. Only by the patient ministry of the Spirit are the ascendant beings of time able to discover the Son.

ch02.s3: The Infinite Spirit, the God of Action
ch02.s3.u1.k: With the personalization of the Infinite Spirit the divine personality cycle is complete and the stage of creation is set.
ch02.s3.u1.p: For the Father's thought and the Son's word to become an actual universe, there must be action. Only when the Third Person is personalized is the cycle of Deity complete and space made ready as a stage for the drama of creation. The Infinite Spirit co-ordinates all energy, spirit, and intellect as the universal unifier.

text: In the eternity of the past, upon the personalization of the Infinite Spirit the divine personality cycle becomes perfect and complete. The God of Action is existent, and the vast stage of space is set for the stupendous drama of creation—the universal adventure—the divine panorama of the eternal ages.

The Conjoint Actor possesses unique prerogatives of synthesis, infinite capacity to co-ordinate all existing universe energies, all actual universe spirits, and all real universe intellects; the Third Source and Center is the universal unifier of the manifold energies and diverse creations which have appeared in consequence of the divine plan and the eternal purpose of the Universal Father.

ch02.s3.u2.k: God is love, the Son is mercy, the Spirit is ministry.
ch02.s3.u2.p: The relation of the three is held in this short sentence. Love is the source; mercy is that love turned toward imperfect beings; ministry is the way mercy becomes an actual touch upon the creature. The Infinite Spirit not only represents Father and Son but also ministers in his own name. Every help we receive expresses this combined love.

text: God is love, the Son is mercy, the Spirit is ministry—the ministry of divine love and endless mercy to all intelligent creation. The Spirit is the personification of the Father's love and the Son's mercy; in him are they eternally united for universal service. The Spirit is love applied to the creature creation, the combined love of the Father and the Son.

To comprehend the ministry of the Spirit, ponder the truth that he is the combined portrayal of the Father's unending love and of the Son's eternal mercy. The Spirit's ministry is not, however, restricted solely to the representation of the Eternal Son and the Universal Father. The Infinite Spirit also possesses the power to minister to the creatures of the realm in his own name and right; the Third Person is of divine dignity and also bestows the universal ministry of mercy in his own behalf.

ch02.s3.u3.k: The Infinite Spirit is not an impersonal force but a divine person who loves and sorrows.
ch02.s3.u3.p: Because the Spirit pervades all things, he is easily imagined as an impersonal influence or energy. The text corrects this misunderstanding. The love of the Spirit is real, and so are his sorrows. The Spirit speaks to us and makes intercession for us. The counsel not to grieve the Spirit has meaning only between persons.

text: "The love of the Spirit" is real, as also are his sorrows; therefore "Grieve not the Spirit of God." Whether we observe the Infinite Spirit as Paradise Deity or as a local universe Creative Spirit, we find that the Conjoint Creator is not only the Third Source and Center but also a divine person. … The Spirit speaks to you, "He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says." "The Spirit himself makes intercession for you."

ch02.s4.u1.k: The Infinite Spirit is the source of mind, and his reality is imperfectly disclosed in human mind.
ch02.s4.u1.p: The Father draws personality, the Son spiritual reality, and the Spirit mind. Man finds the Third Person comparatively easy to conceive because the very mind with which he thinks comes from him. All true thoughts and perfect ideas are drawn into the absolute mind circuit. An intellect that loves truth is already answering the Spirit's pull.

text: Since the Third Person of Deity is the source of mind, it is quite natural that the evolutionary will creatures find it easier to form comprehensible concepts of the Infinite Spirit than they do of either the Eternal Son or the Universal Father. The reality of the Conjoint Creator is disclosed imperfectly in the very existence of human mind.

Much as the Father draws all personality to himself, and as the Son attracts all spiritual reality, so does the Conjoint Actor exercise a drawing power on all minds; he unqualifiedly dominates and controls the universal mind circuit. All true and genuine intellectual values, all divine thoughts and perfect ideas, are unerringly drawn into this absolute circuit of mind.

ch02.s4.u2.k: Though the source of mind is divine, man's immature intellect should evoke humility.
ch02.s4.u2.p: That mind comes from the Infinite Spirit does not make every human thought divine. The text speaks frankly of how easily insincerity, unrighteousness, animal fear, and useless anxiety mar the mind. Mind turns spirit values into meanings, and will brings those meanings to fruit. To tend the mind is to prepare the path of ascent.

text: Too often, all too often, you mar your minds by insincerity and sear them with unrighteousness; you subject them to animal fear and distort them by useless anxiety. Therefore, though the source of mind is divine, mind as you know it on your world of ascension can hardly become the object of great admiration, much less of adoration or worship. The contemplation of the immature and inactive human intellect should lead only to reactions of humility.
Mind transmutes the values of spirit into the meanings of intellect; volition has power to bring the meanings of mind to fruit in both the material and spiritual domains.

ch02.qs1: When have I experienced God's love in the concrete forms of mercy and ministry?
ch02.qs2: How much of my praying carries the kind of spiritual value the spirit-gravity circuit receives?
ch02.qs3: What can I do today to guard my mind, which comes from the Infinite Spirit, from insincerity and anxiety?
ch03.sub: The Eternal Union of Undivided Deity
ch03.sum: Deity is one, yet there are three positive and divine personalizations of Deity. The Paradise Trinity springs from the self-sharing, loving nature of the Universal Father and exists as the eternal Deity union of Father, Son, and Spirit. The Trinity is not merely the sum of three persons but undivided Deity, and it performs collective functions, such as justice, judgment, and the administration of totality, which belong to no single person. This chapter asks why the Trinity is inevitable, what the union of the three persons means, how justice and mercy go together, and how mankind has received this truth.
ch03.s1.u1.k: Divine personality is not self-centered; from eternity the Father has distributed himself.
ch03.s1.u1.p: The starting point for understanding the Trinity is not arithmetic but character. The Universal Father keeps only what cannot be delegated and gives everything else away, because love does not remain alone. As creatures crave fellowship with other persons, so the Infinite shares reality of being and equality of self with two co-ordinate persons. The Trinity is the shape self-giving love has taken in eternity.

text: It would seem that the Father, back in eternity, inaugurated a policy of profound self-distribution. There is inherent in the selfless, loving, and lovable nature of the Universal Father something which causes him to reserve to himself the exercise of only those powers and that authority which he apparently finds it impossible to delegate or to bestow.

Divine personality is not self-centered; self-distribution and sharing of personality characterize divine freewill selfhood. Creatures crave association with other personal creatures; Creators are moved to share divinity with their universe children; the personality of the Infinite is disclosed as the Universal Father, who shares reality of being and equality of self with two co-ordinate personalities, the Eternal Son and the Conjoint Actor.

ch03.s1.u2.k: The Son is indispensable to God's fatherhood, the Spirit to the fraternity of Son and Spirit.
ch03.s1.u2.p: To be a father there must be a son, and to be a brother there must be another companion. Divine relationship thus holds fatherhood and brotherhood together. The text notes that three persons form a minimum social group, yet adds that this is the least of the reasons. The plural in "Let us make man in our own image" points to this relationship within the one Deity.

text: The Son is indispensable to the fatherhood of God. The Spirit is indispensable to the fraternity of the Second and Third Persons. Three persons are a minimum social group, but this is least of all the many reasons for believing in the inevitability of the Conjoint Actor.

Notwithstanding there is only one Deity, there are three positive and divine personalizations of Deity. Regarding the endowment of man with the divine Adjusters, the Father said: "Let us make mortal man in our own image." Repeatedly throughout the Urantian writings there occurs this reference to the acts and doings of plural Deity, clearly showing recognition of the existence and working of the three Sources and Centers.

ch03.s1.u3.k: The Sons are the Word of God; the children of the Spirit are the Act of God.
ch03.s1.u3.p: The three persons are equal in nature and co-ordinate in being, yet their universe work is clearly distinct. God speaks through the Son and, with the Son, acts through the Spirit. Son and Spirit work like two brothers who share one honored Father. That the inner life of Deity is not rivalry but admiration and love is a pattern for every relationship among creatures.

text: The divine Sons are indeed the "Word of God," but the children of the Spirit are truly the "Act of God." God speaks through the Son and, with the Son, acts through the Infinite Spirit, while in all universe activities the Son and the Spirit are exquisitely fraternal, working as two equal brothers with admiration and love for an honored and divinely respected common Father.

The Father, Son, and Spirit are certainly equal in nature, co-ordinate in being, but there are unmistakable differences in their universe performances, and when acting alone, each person of Deity is apparently limited in absoluteness.

ch03.s2.u1.k: Eternal Deity is perfectly unified, yet exists as three perfectly individualized persons.
ch03.s2.u1.p: The Trinity makes diversity and unity possible at the same time. The three persons each have their own character and powers and may collaborate as they choose, yet such collaboration is not the Trinity. The Trinity is real as the Deity union of the three, and the Father, the Son, or the Spirit can each sustain a relationship to it. Union does not erase personality.

text: Eternal Deity is perfectly unified; nevertheless there are three perfectly individualized persons of Deity. The Paradise Trinity makes possible the simultaneous expression of all the diversity of the character traits and infinite powers of the First Source and Center and his eternal co-ordinates and of all the divine unity of the universe functions of undivided Deity.

The Paradise Trinity is real. It exists as the Deity union of Father, Son, and Spirit; yet the Father, the Son, or the Spirit, or any two of them, can function in relation to this selfsame Paradise Trinity. The Father, Son, and Spirit can collaborate in a non-Trinity manner, but not as three Deities. As persons they can collaborate as they choose, but that is not the Trinity.

ch03.s2.u2.k: The Trinity is not a functional unanimity but undivided and indivisible Deity.
ch03.s2.u2.p: Three people working with one mind is different from three being one Deity. The text calls the functional union of the three persons a triunity and says the Trinity is something else: undivided Deity. This distinction guards against two misunderstandings at once, the Trinity as a committee of three Gods and the Trinity as three masks of one God.

text: The Paradise Trinity is not a triunity; it is not a functional unanimity; rather is it undivided and indivisible Deity. The Father, Son, and Spirit (as persons) can sustain a relationship to the Paradise Trinity, for the Trinity is their undivided Deity.

ch03.s2.u3.k: Mortals view the Trinity according to their own enlightenment and discover more of it as they ascend.
ch03.s2.u3.p: The Trinity is not an examination question to be mastered now. The text counsels mortals in the flesh to view it according to their own enlightenment and the responses of mind and soul. We know little now, but on the way to Paradise there will be repeated and astonishing discoveries. Humility before the mystery and expectation of discovery go together.

text: As a mortal in the flesh you should view the Trinity in accordance with your individual enlightenment and in harmony with the reactions of your mind and soul. You can know very little of the absoluteness of the Trinity, but as you ascend Paradiseward, you will many times experience astonishment at successive revelations and unexpected discoveries of Trinity supremacy and ultimacy, if not of absoluteness.

ch03.s3.u1.k: Justice is never the attitude of a single person; it is always a plural function.
ch03.s3.u1.p: Father, Son, and Spirit are persons of love, mercy, and ministry, and none of them administers justice alone. Justice appears only as a collective function when the three unite as the Trinity. Jesus' teaching that justice is a group function, never a personal act, rests on the same principle. This is why human communities set public judgment in place of private revenge.

text: Justice is not the attitude of the Father, the Son, or the Spirit. Justice is the Trinity attitude of these personalities of love, mercy, and ministry. No one of the Paradise Deities fosters the administration of justice. Justice is never a personal attitude; it is always a plural function.

For example: The Master, when on earth, admonished his followers that justice is never a personal act; it is always a group function. Neither do the Gods, as persons, administer justice. But they perform this very function as a collective whole, as the Paradise Trinity.

ch03.s3.u2.k: Justice is the collective thought of righteousness; mercy is its personal expression.
ch03.s3.u2.p: People easily feel that justice and mercy collide. The text says that, when fully understood, the righteous justice of the Trinity and the merciful love of the Father coincide. Because man lacks that understanding, the three persons in the universes of time are adjusted to a co-ordinate ministry of love and law. Justice does not oppose love; it guards love's order.

text: Justice is the collective thought of righteousness; mercy is its personal expression. … When fully perceived and completely understood, the righteous justice of the Trinity and the merciful love of the Universal Father are coincident. But man has no such full understanding of divine justice. Thus in the Trinity, as man would view it, the personalities of Father, Son, and Spirit are adjusted to co-ordinate ministry of love and law in the experiential universes of time.

ch03.s3.u3.k: Even life's inexplicable vicissitudes may be woven into a meaningful pattern under Trinity overcontrol.
ch03.s3.u3.p: Before disasters, illnesses, and accidents, people ask about the will of God. Instead of a firm answer the text offers a possibility: the inexplicable vicissitudes of living may be interwoven into a meaningful pattern of high value by the function of the Supreme and the overcontrol of the Trinity. We can discern personal love in the Father's acts, but the full meaning of the Trinity's acts is disclosed only in eternity.

text: It may be that the circumstances of existence and the inexplicable vicissitudes of living are all interwoven into a meaningful pattern of high value by the function of the Supreme and the overcontrol of the Trinity.

As a son of God you can discern the personal attitude of love in all the acts of God the Father. But you will not always be able to understand how many of the universe acts of the Paradise Trinity redound to the good of the individual mortal on the evolutionary worlds of space. In the progress of eternity the acts of the Trinity will be revealed as altogether meaningful and considerate, but they do not always so appear to the creatures of time.

ch03.s4.u1.k: Jesus taught the truth of the Trinity, but his apostles heard it only as a figure of speech.
ch03.s4.u1.p: Mankind has long been at home with the number three; triad ideas grew from natural experiences like finger joints and stool legs. Yet the revealed Trinity is different from such triad beliefs. When Jesus taught this truth, his apostles, bound by Hebraic monotheism, received it only as symbol. Truth is passed on only in the measure of the mind that receives it.

text: THE Trinity concept of revealed religion must not be confused with the triad beliefs of evolutionary religions. The ideas of triads arose from many suggestive relationships but chiefly because of the three joints of the fingers, because three legs were the fewest which could stabilize a stool, because three support points could keep up a tent; furthermore, primitive man, for a long time, could not count beyond three.

Jesus taught his apostles the truth regarding the persons of the Paradise Trinity, but they thought he spoke figuratively and symbolically. Having been nurtured in Hebraic monotheism, they found it difficult to entertain any belief that seemed to conflict with their dominating concept of Yahweh.

ch03.s4.u2.k: Through the Trinity concept man can grasp how love and law go together in the universe.
ch03.s4.u2.p: Faith brings insight into the love of God, yet that faith does not alter the laws of the material universe, and meeting this fact can be bewildering. The text offers the Trinity concept as the key. Through it man can begin to grasp how love and law interrelate in the time-space creations. Love and law are two faces of the same Deity.

text: Through the recognition of the Trinity concept the mind of man can hope to grasp something of the interrelationship of love and law in the time-space creations. Through spiritual faith man gains insight into the love of God but soon discovers that this spiritual faith has no influence on the ordained laws of the material universe.

ch03.qs1: What does the self-sharing character of God ask of my relationships and my way of giving?
ch03.qs2: If justice is a group function rather than a personal attitude, how might I deal differently with grievance and anger?
ch03.qs3: What do I need in order to keep trusting while admitting that I do not yet understand some suffering?
ch04.sub: The Supreme Being and the Ultimate
ch04.sum: The Father, the Son, and the Spirit are existential Deity, eternal from the beginning. Yet The Urantia Book also reveals Deity that grows in time: experiential Deity. God the Supreme is even now actualizing as the synthesis of the experience of all Creators and creatures in the grand universe, and God the Ultimate is emerging on the time-transcended levels of the master universe. This truth casts new light on suffering and inequality, and it carries the astonishing meaning that human choice and effort actually take part in the growth of God. This chapter considers the idea of experiential Deity, the nature of the Supreme Being, the relation of the Supreme to man, and the endless quest beyond the Ultimate.
ch04.s1.u1.k: Father, Son, and Spirit are existential; the Supreme, the Ultimate, and the Absolute are actualizing experiential Deity.
ch04.s1.u1.p: The Urantia Book's teaching about Deity runs in two lines. On one side stand the eternal Gods who were, are, and ever will be unchanged. On the other stand the Deities who actualize through experience as the universe grows. God the Supreme, God the Ultimate, and God the Absolute are such actualizing Deity personalities. Time becomes a meaningful stage even for God.

text: God the Father, God the Son, and God the Spirit are eternal—are existential beings—while God the Supreme, God the Ultimate, and God the Absolute are actualizing Deity personalities of the post-Havona epochs in the time-space and the time-space-transcended spheres of master universe evolutionary expansion.

ch04.s1.u2.k: Growth is the earmark of experiential Deity and implies partnership between God and man.
ch04.s1.u2.p: Havona does not grow, for it was perfect from the beginning. But the universes of time grow, and in that growth Creator and creature work together. Once we see that our immediate Creators are divine and yet finite, inequality and suffering appear not as the indifference of the Infinite but as signs of an unfinished joint work. Faith is then no longer used to counsel resignation.

text: Experiential growth implies creature-Creator partnership—God and man in association. Growth is the earmark of experiential Deity: Havona did not grow; Havona is and always has been; it is existential like the everlasting Gods who are its source. But growth characterizes the grand universe.

IF MAN recognized that his Creators—his immediate supervisors—while being divine were also finite, and that the God of time and space was an evolving and nonabsolute Deity, then would the inconsistencies of temporal inequalities cease to be profound religious paradoxes. No longer would religious faith be prostituted to the promotion of social smugness in the fortunate while serving only to encourage stoical resignation in the unfortunate victims of social deprivation.

ch04.s2: The Supreme Being, God in Time
ch04.s2.u1.k: The Supreme is God-in-time, and the secret of creature growth lies in him.
ch04.s2.u1.p: For man, to exist is to grow. The text says this growth is not an accident but a function of the Supreme Being. The conquest of the incomplete present, the consummation of the perfecting future, and the coming of power under the control of spirit through mind all take place in the Supreme. Our daily experience of growth is part of the larger story of a growing universe.

text: The Supreme is God-in-time; his is the secret of creature growth in time; his also is the conquest of the incomplete present and the consummation of the perfecting future. And the final fruits of all finite growth are: power controlled through mind by spirit by virtue of the unifying and creative presence of personality. The culminating consequence of all this growth is the Supreme Being.

To mortal man, existence is equivalent to growth. And so indeed it would seem to be, even in the larger universe sense, for spirit-led existence does seem to result in experiential growth—augmentation of status. We have long held, however, that the present growth which characterizes creature existence in the present universe age is a function of the Supreme.

ch04.s2.u2.k: God the Supreme is truth, beauty, and goodness, the oversoul of the finite cosmos.
ch04.s2.u2.p: When a person grasps what is true, is moved by what is beautiful, and chooses what is good, he is touching the reality of God the Supreme. Truth, beauty, and goodness are the finite maximums of divinity that a creature can experience. The Supreme is not a distant abstraction but the sweetness of true success and the joy of everlasting achievement. Every good moment of life points toward him.

text: The Supreme is the beauty of physical harmony, the truth of intellectual meaning, and the goodness of spiritual value. He is the sweetness of true success and the joy of everlasting achievement. He is the oversoul of the grand universe, the consciousness of the finite cosmos, the completion of finite reality, and the personification of Creator-creature experience.

Truth, beauty, and goodness are correlated in the ministry of the Spirit, the grandeur of Paradise, the mercy of the Son, and the experience of the Supreme. God the Supreme is truth, beauty, and goodness, for these concepts of divinity represent finite maximums of ideational experience.

ch04.s2.u3.k: In the Supreme Being, Creator and creature are united in one Deity.
ch04.s2.u3.p: The will of the Creator and the will of the creature are qualitatively different, yet they are akin in that they can work together. Man collaborates with God to cocreate an eternal finaliter, and God works as humanity in the incarnations of his Sons. As Michael's will, joining divinity and humanity, is more than the sum of the two, so the will of the Supreme is a new reality beyond either Creator or creature.

text: The will of the Creator and the will of the creature are qualitatively different, but they are also experientially akin, for creature and Creator can collaborate in the achievement of universe perfection. Man can work in liaison with God and thereby cocreate an eternal finaliter. God can work even as humanity in the incarnations of his Sons, who thereby achieve the supremacy of creature experience.

In the Supreme Being, Creator and creature are united in one Deity whose will is expressive of one divine personality. And this will of the Supreme is something more than the will of either creature or Creator, even as the sovereign will of the Master Son of Nebadon is now something more than a combination of the will of divinity and humanity. The union of Paradise perfection and time-space experience yields a new meaning value on deity levels of reality.

ch04.s3.u1.k: As we do the will of God, the almighty potential of the Supreme becomes one step more actual.
ch04.s3.u1.p: Doing the will of God does not remain a matter of private piety. It is a step added to the actualization of Deity in the universe. The Father planned that finite progress should rest on effort, achievement on perseverance, and personality growth on faith. So no small act of obedience is wasted; it is recorded forever in the growth of the Supreme.

text: TO THE extent that we do the will of God in whatever universe station we may have our existence, in that measure the almighty potential of the Supreme becomes one step more actual. … And God the Supreme is becoming the highest finite manifestation of the total will of God.

All this must be according to the Father's plan, which has predicated finite progress upon effort, creature achievement upon perseverance, and personality development upon faith. By thus ordaining the experience-evolution of the Supreme, the Father has made it possible for finite creatures to exist in the universes and, by experiential progression, sometime to attain the divinity of Supremacy.

ch04.s3.u2.k: God trusts man enough to place a portion of his divine nature in human hands.
ch04.s3.u2.p: The Father's nature, present as the Thought Adjuster, cannot be destroyed whatever man chooses. But the evolving self, the child of the Supreme, can be lost. God knows this risk and still entrusts himself to man. As we strive for self-realization, the Supreme strives in us and with us. Human growth and divine growth are not separate.

text: God is so trusting, so loving, that he gives a portion of his divine nature into the hands of even human beings for safekeeping and self-realization. The Father nature, the Adjuster presence, is indestructible regardless of the choice of the mortal being. The child of the Supreme, the evolving self, can be destroyed notwithstanding that the potentially unifying personality of such a misguided self will persist as a factor of the Deity of Supremacy.

And so, as we strive for self-expression, the Supreme is striving in us, and with us, for deity expression. As we find the Father, so has the Supreme again found the Paradise Creator of all things. As we master the problems of self-realization, so is the God of experience achieving almighty supremacy in the universes of time and space.

ch04.s3.u3.k: Before each person lies the decision whether to fail the God of time, who depends on every creature.
ch04.s3.u3.p: This passage is one of the most urgent appeals in the whole revelation. The Supreme is the great brother of all creatures and depends on the decision of each one. Whether to fail the God of time and the Supreme personality of the universes through the slothfulness of animalistic retrogression rests with each person. The revelator confesses having once faced the same decision.

text: And so the decision awaits each of you as it once awaited each of us: Will you fail the God of time, who is so dependent upon the decisions of the finite mind? will you fail the Supreme personality of the universes by the slothfulness of animalistic retrogression? will you fail the great brother of all creatures, who is so dependent on each creature?

ch04.s3.u4.k: Man finds the Father in his own heart, but must seek the Supreme in the hearts of all other men.
ch04.s3.u4.p: Meeting the Father happens within the individual, but meeting the Supreme happens in relationship and community. When all creatures fully reveal the love of the Supreme, he becomes a universe actuality. And this discovery is not dramatic but slow and steady, like a river wearing away the soil. To love one's neighbor is also to seek God the Supreme.

text: Man can discover the Father in his heart, but he will have to search for the Supreme in the hearts of all other men; and when all creatures perfectly reveal the love of the Supreme, then will he become a universe actuality to all creatures. And that is just another way of saying that the universes will be settled in light and life.
Men do not find the Supreme suddenly and spectacularly as an earthquake tears chasms into the rocks, but they find him slowly and patiently as a river quietly wears away the soil beneath.

ch04.s4: The Ultimate and the Endless Quest
ch04.s4.u1.k: God the Ultimate is supersupreme Deity functioning on levels that transcend time and space.
ch04.s4.u1.p: If the Supreme is the Trinity unification comprehended by finite beings, the Ultimate is the unification comprehended by absonite beings beyond time and space. To man this is remote, yet the text says that every personality who has taken part in actualizing this Deity level will experience the values of its transcendental divinity. The way beyond the finite leads to ultimate attainment.

text: God the Ultimate is designative of personal Deity functioning on the divinity levels of the absonite and on the universe spheres of supertime and transcended space. The Ultimate is a supersupreme eventuation of Deity. The Supreme is the Trinity unification comprehended by finite beings; the Ultimate is the unification of the Paradise Trinity comprehended by absonite beings.

But irrespective of the administrative repercussions attendant upon the emergence of Ultimate Deity, the personal values of his transcendental divinity will be experiencible by all personalities who have been participants in the actualization of this Deity level. Transcendence of the finite can lead only to ultimate attainment. God the Ultimate exists in transcendence of time and space but is nonetheless subabsolute notwithstanding inherent capacity for functional association with absolutes.

ch04.s4.u2.k: The infinity of God is not a cause for discouragement but the supreme assurance of endless growth.
ch04.s4.u2.p: That we can never fully attain God sounds at first like a defeat, but the text reads it the opposite way. The infinity of God is the supreme assurance that before the ascending personality lie possibilities of personality development and Deity association that even eternity will not exhaust. Endlessness is not monotony but the promise that new discovery always awaits.

text: Far from harassing the creature, the infinity of God should be the supreme assurance that throughout all endless futurity an ascending personality will have before him the possibilities of personality development and Deity association which even eternity will neither exhaust nor terminate.

ch04.s4.u3.k: A life of living the Father's will leads directly to the attainment of spirit supremacy.
ch04.s4.u3.p: The lofty philosophy of experiential Deity returns at last to a very concrete life: one founded on truth, sensitive to beauty, and ruled by goodness. Such a life of the Father's will is itself the way to spirit supremacy, a step nearer to comprehending the Father-Infinite.

text: To material, evolutionary, finite creatures, a life predicated on the living of the Father's will leads directly to the attainment of spirit supremacy in the personality arena and brings such creatures one step nearer the comprehension of the Father-Infinite. Such a Father life is one predicated on truth, sensitive to beauty, and dominated by goodness.

ch04.qs1: How does the teaching that God grows in time change the way I see my own imperfection and suffering?
ch04.qs2: If some small act of doing God's will today has been added to the growth of the Supreme, what was it?
ch04.qs3: What would it mean in my relationships to seek God the Supreme in the hearts of others?
ch05.sub: The I AM and the Seven Absolutes of Infinity
ch05.sum: At the deepest foundation of its teaching about God, The Urantia Book places the philosophic postulate of the I AM. All reality has its origin in the infinite I AM, and the seven prime relationships within the I AM eternalize as the Seven Absolutes of Infinity. Among them the Deity Absolute, the Unqualified Absolute, and the Universal Absolute make up the realm of potential not yet actualized. This chapter considers the concept of the I AM and the Seven Absolutes, the nature of the three Absolutes of potential, how the Absolutes are unified, and what they mean for providence in the universe and for human faith. Even before infinity, the face man meets is always that of a loving Father.
ch05.s1.u1.k: All reality originates in the infinite I AM, and the face he turns toward us is the face of a Father.
ch05.s1.u1.p: The finite mind can think only by imagining a beginning, so the revelation offers as its first philosophic postulate the solitary infinity that precedes all reality, the I AM. The idea sounds cold and remote, yet the text at once adds that infinity can limit itself and be expressed on every level. And the face that infinity shows to persons is that of a loving Father.

text: The I AM is the Infinite; the I AM is also infinity. From the sequential, time viewpoint, all reality has its origin in the infinite I AM, whose solitary existence in past infinite eternity must be a finite creature's premier philosophic postulate.

Unqualified infinity is meaningless to the finite creature, but infinity is capable of self-limitation and is susceptible of reality expression to all levels of universe existences. And the face which the Infinite turns toward all universe personalities is the face of a Father, the Universal Father of love.

ch05.s1.u2.k: The Father we experience is a phase of the Infinite; the I AM remains our hypothesis of all that is unknowable.
ch05.s1.u2.p: This distinction protects the place of both faith and philosophy. The God whom the worshiping mind meets is the Father actually experienced in personality. Yet beyond him lies all that we feel to be unknowable about the First Source and Center. The concept of the I AM is an honest name for that unknowableness. We may love as far as we know and be humble as far as we do not.

text: Ever remember that man's comprehension of the Universal Father is a personal experience. … God, your Father and my Father, is that phase of the Infinite which we perceive in our personalities as an actual experiential reality, but the I AM ever remains as our hypothesis of all that we feel is unknowable of the First Source and Center.

ch05.s2.u1.k: The seven prime relationships within the I AM eternalize as the Seven Absolutes, the premise of reality.
ch05.s2.u1.p: The seven Absolutes are the Universal Father, the Eternal Son, the Isle of Paradise, the Infinite Spirit, and the Deity, Unqualified, and Universal Absolutes. Man can only describe them as if they arose in sequence, but in fact all are co-ordinately eternal. Even the idea that the First Source and Center precedes all others is only a helpful postulate that yields before the fact of eternal coexistence.

text: The seven prime relationships within the I AM eternalize as the Seven Absolutes of Infinity. But though we may portray reality origins and infinity differentiation by a sequential narrative, in fact all seven Absolutes are unqualifiedly and co-ordinately eternal. … The seven Absolutes are the premise of reality.

The Seven Absolutes of Infinity constitute the beginnings of reality. As mortal minds would regard it, the First Source and Center would appear to be antecedent to all absolutes. But such a postulate, however helpful, is invalidated by the eternity coexistence of the Son, the Spirit, the three Absolutes, and the Paradise Isle.

ch05.s2.u2.k: The Deity Absolute is the totality of all Deity potential, the destiny inceptor.
ch05.s2.u2.p: The Deity Absolute is the realm of potential segregated from total infinite reality by the Father's freewill choice. All divinity activity, existential or experiential, takes place within it. Because the unrealized possibilities of Deity lie here, the Deity Absolute is called the destiny inceptor. The growth of the Supreme and the Ultimate is in the end this potential turning into actuality.

text: 5. The Deity Absolute. The causational, potentially personal possibilities of universal reality, the totality of all Deity potential. The Deity Absolute is the purposive qualifier of the unqualified, absolute, and nondeity realities. The Deity Absolute is the qualifier of the absolute and the absolutizer of the qualified—the destiny inceptor.

The Deity Absolute is that potential which was segregated from total, infinite reality by the freewill choice of the Universal Father, and within which all divinity activities—existential and experiential—take place. This is the Qualified Absolute in contradistinction to the Unqualified Absolute; but the Universal Absolute is superadditive to both in the encompassment of all absolute potential.

ch05.s2.u3.k: The Unqualified Absolute is the finality of nonpersonal potential, yet not a vague pantheistic influence.
ch05.s2.u3.p: The Unqualified Absolute is the totality of nondeified reality, without personality or divinity. Its presence is limitless, and even eternity cannot exhaust its quiescence. Yet the revelators state clearly that it should not be seen as an undifferentiated, all-pervading influence like the pantheism of metaphysics or the ether of older science. It is force unlimited and yet Deity conditioned.

text: The Unqualified Absolute. Static, reactive, and abeyant; the unrevealed cosmic infinity of the I AM; totality of nondeified reality and finality of all nonpersonal potential. … There is a concept periphery to the master universe, but the presence of the Unqualified is limitless; even eternity cannot exhaust the boundless quiescence of this nondeity Absolute.

We are convinced that the Unqualified Absolute is not an undifferentiated and all-pervading influence comparable either to the pantheistic concepts of metaphysics or to the sometime ether hypothesis of science. The Unqualified Absolute is force unlimited and Deity conditioned, but we do not fully perceive the relation of this Absolute to the spirit realities of the universes.

ch05.s2.u4.k: Because of the presence of the Universal Absolute, the finite can coexist with the Infinite.
ch05.s2.u4.p: How can a small creature exist beside the Infinite? The text answers: the Universal Absolute. This Absolute equalizes the tensions between time and eternity, finite and infinite, man and God, and so makes room for evolving reality to grow. Nor is the Absolute a self-determining impersonal deity; in all that concerns personality it is under the rule of the Trinity.

text: The finite can coexist in the cosmos along with the Infinite only because the associative presence of the Universal Absolute so perfectly equalizes the tensions between time and eternity, finity and infinity, reality potential and reality actuality, Paradise and space, man and God.

We never use the term the Absolute as a negation of aught or as a denial of anything. Neither do we regard the Universal Absolute as self-determinative, a sort of pantheistic and impersonal Deity. The Absolute, in all that pertains to universe personality, is strictly Trinity limited and Deity dominated.

ch05.s3.u1.k: On subinfinite levels there are three Absolutes, but in infinity they are one, and all things center in the Paradise Father.
ch05.s3.u1.p: The intricate account of the Absolutes finally converges in unity. The three Absolutes are one in the Universal Absolute and reach the worlds of time and space through the Ultimate, the Supreme, and God the Sevenfold. As the three persons of Paradise are one in the Trinity, so all reality is bound together. God is all and in all, and nothing exists without him.

text: The Unqualified Absolute and the Deity Absolute are unified in the Universal Absolute. The Absolutes are co-ordinated in the Ultimate, conditioned in the Supreme, and time-space modified in God the Sevenfold. On subinfinite levels there are three Absolutes, but in infinity they appear to be one. On Paradise there are three personalizations of Deity, but in the Trinity they are one.

The universe of universes is altogether unified. … Philosophically and experientially, in concept and in reality, all things and beings center in the Paradise Father. God is all and in all, and no things or beings exist without him.

ch05.s3.u2.k: Whatever Deity level we reach, we rediscover each time the Paradise Father of all personalities.
ch05.s3.u2.p: The names God the Sevenfold, God the Supreme, God the Ultimate, and God the Absolute do not lead man into a maze of strange gods. At the close of each adventure the ascender meets the same One again on a new level of experience: the eternal Father. Even the long journey of grasping at the concept of the Absolute is in the end a way home to the Father.

text: As personalities, now or in the successive universe experiences of the eternal future, no matter if you achieve the attainment of God the Sevenfold, comprehend God the Supreme, find God the Ultimate, or attempt to grasp the concept of God the Absolute, you will discover to your eternal satisfaction that in the consummation of each adventure you have, on new experiential levels, rediscovered the eternal God—the Paradise Father of all universe personalities.

ch05.s4.u1.k: Providence is the realm of the Supreme Being and the Conjoint Actor, guiding confused phenomena to God's glory and man's good.
ch05.s4.u1.p: There are moments in life when apparently unrelated events fit together astonishingly. The text explains this as providence, the way the living presence of the evolving Supreme Being becomes manifest. Providence is not a fatalism that fixes every event in advance; it is a far-flung and mostly unrecognized control co-ordinating all universe activity, so that mixed phenomena finally work out for good.

text: There is also an organic unity in the universes of time and space which seems to underlie the whole fabric of cosmic events. This living presence of the evolving Supreme Being, this Immanence of the Projected Incomplete, is inexplicably manifested ever and anon by what appears to be an amazingly fortuitous co-ordination of apparently unrelated universe happenings. This must be the function of Providence—the realm of the Supreme Being and the Conjoint Actor.

I am inclined to believe that it is this far-flung and generally unrecognizable control of the co-ordination and interassociation of all phases and forms of universe activity that causes such a variegated and apparently hopelessly confused medley of physical, mental, moral, and spiritual phenomena so unerringly to work out to the glory of God and for the good of men and angels.

ch05.s4.u2.k: Because of the Absolutes, the universe is never wholly predictable, and apparent accidents belong to the adventure of the Infinite.
ch05.s4.u2.p: Neither scientist, philosopher, nor religionist can fully predict how the universe will respond. The text traces this to the not-fully-revealed presence of the Absolutes. This is not a confession of disorder but a confession that the universe is not a closed machine. What looks to us like accident belongs, from a larger view, to the time-space drama the Infinite is unfolding.

text: These Absolutes must be the not-fully-revealed presences abroad in the universe which, in the phenomena of space potency and in the function of other superultimates, render it impossible for physicists, philosophers, or even religionists to predict with certainty as to just how the primordials of force, concept, or spirit will respond to demands made in a complex reality situation involving supreme adjustments and ultimate values.
But in the larger sense the apparent "accidents" of the cosmos are undoubtedly a part of the finite drama of the time-space adventure of the Infinite in his eternal manipulation of the Absolutes.

ch05.s4.u3.k: However much of God we attain, much more remains; the quest for God is endless.
ch05.s4.u3.p: At the end of the teaching about the Absolutes, man stands before the depth of infinity. However much of God he attains, there will always remain much more of him. This is not a cause for despair but for joy. A God fully known would leave nothing to seek, but the infinite God grants new discovery throughout eternity.

text: No matter how much of God you may attain, there will always remain much more of him, the existence of which you will not even suspect. … The quest for God is endless!

ch05.qs1: Does admitting what I do not know before the infinite God weaken my faith or deepen it?
ch05.qs2: If I have known events that seemed unrelated but later fit together meaningfully, how might I reread them in the light of providence?
ch05.qs3: What expectation and attitude does the endlessness of the quest for God awaken in my daily life?
ch06.sub: The Eternal Isle at the Center of the Universe of Universes
ch06.sum: The cosmology of The Urantia Book begins from a single center. Paradise is the eternal dwelling place of the Universal Father, the Eternal Son, and the Infinite Spirit, and at the same time the most gigantic organized body of cosmic reality in the master universe. Paradise is a spiritual abode and a literal place, the source of all energy and matter, and the center of universal gravity. It is the absolute pattern beyond time and space, and also the destination toward which every God-knowing mortal is bound. This chapter considers Paradise in turn as the Father's house, as the nonpersonal center of reality, as the source of energy and gravity, and as the goal of all personalities.
ch06.s1.u1.k: Paradise is the eternal center of the universe of universes, a spiritual abode and a material sphere.
ch06.s1.u1.p: Unlike traditions that think of God's dwelling only as a vague heaven, The Urantia Book reveals Paradise as a real place. Because all intelligent creatures live on material abodes, the absolute controlling center of the universe must also be material and literal. At the same time the text insists that spirit things and spirit beings are just as real. On Paradise, matter and spirit are not opposed.

text: PARADISE is the eternal center of the universe of universes and the abiding place of the Universal Father, the Eternal Son, the Infinite Spirit, and their divine co-ordinates and associates. … Paradise is a material sphere as well as a spiritual abode. All of the intelligent creation of the Universal Father is domiciled on material abodes; hence must the absolute controlling center also be material, literal. And again it should be reiterated that spirit things and spiritual beings are real.

ch06.s1.u2.k: God dwells in this central and eternal abode, and there he is always to be found.
ch06.s1.u2.p: God is everywhere, yet he also dwells personally in one place. At the center of upper Paradise is the personal presence of the Father, surrounded by the presence of the Son, and both are invested by the glory of the Spirit. That God is always found in the same place gives every pilgrim of the universe a sure direction that cannot be lost.

text: The personal presence of the Universal Father is resident at the very center of the upper surface of this well-nigh circular, but not spherical, abode of the Deities. This Paradise presence of the Universal Father is immediately surrounded by the personal presence of the Eternal Son, while they are both invested by the unspeakable glory of the Infinite Spirit.

God dwells, has dwelt, and everlastingly will dwell in this same central and eternal abode. We have always found him there and always will. The Universal Father is cosmically focalized, spiritually personalized, and geographically resident at this center of the universe of universes.

ch06.s1.u3.k: Paradise is the Father's House, and mansions are prepared there for ascending creatures.
ch06.s1.u3.p: The old promise of many mansions in the Father's house takes concrete shape here. The Holy Area of Paradise is divided into seven concentric zones, and these are the Father's Paradise mansions. Yet the revelator stops short of describing its glory further. Man must wait, and ascend while he waits.

text: The Holy Area, the outlying or residential region, is divided into seven concentric zones. Paradise is sometimes called "the Father's House" since it is his eternal residence, and these seven zones are often designated "the Father's Paradise mansions."

But a further attempt to visualize to you the glories of Paradise would be futile. You must wait, and ascend while you wait, for truly, "Eye has not seen, nor ear heard, neither has it entered into the mind of mortal man, the things which the Universal Father has prepared for those who survive the life in the flesh on the worlds of time and space."

ch06.s2.u1.k: The substance of Paradise is neither dead nor alive; it is the original nonspiritual expression of the First Source and Center.
ch06.s2.u1.p: The substance of Paradise is a stationary system of reality, a homogeneous organization of space potency found nowhere else in the universe. It is neither life nor death but the Father's first expression of himself in a nonspiritual way. That all the matter of the universe is rooted at last in this pattern reminds us that the material world, too, comes from God.

text: The eternal Isle is composed of a single form of materialization—stationary systems of reality. This literal substance of Paradise is a homogeneous organization of space potency not to be found elsewhere in all the wide universe of universes. … This Paradise source material is neither dead nor alive; it is the original nonspiritual expression of the First Source and Center; it is Paradise, and Paradise is without duplicate.

ch06.s2.u2.k: Paradise is nonspatial, and time is not a feature of Paradise existence.
ch06.s2.u2.p: All human thought moves within the frame of time and space, but Paradise lies outside that frame. Paradise is nonspatial, and time as we know it is not a feature of its existence. Its citizens are conscious of nontime sequence, and motion there is volitional. That the ground of time and space lies beyond time and space is worth long meditation.

text: Time, as you understand it, is not a feature of Paradise existence, though the citizens of the central Isle are fully conscious of nontime sequence of events. Motion is not inherent on Paradise; it is volitional. … Paradise is nonspatial; hence its areas are absolute and therefore serviceable in many ways beyond the concept of mortal mind.

ch06.s2.u3.k: The Father revealed his personal self in the Son and, at the same time, his nonpersonal self as Paradise.
ch06.s2.u3.p: The Eternal Son and Paradise are two faces of the same moment. When the Father expressed his spirit self as the Son, the infinite potential of his nonpersonal self appeared as Paradise; thus the Father projected reality in two phases, the personal and the nonpersonal, the spiritual and the nonspiritual. Paradise is no creator and no ancestor of any being, yet as the absolute of patterns it upholds the order of the universe.

text: In the eternity of the past, when the Universal Father gave infinite personality expression of his spirit self in the being of the Eternal Son, simultaneously he revealed the infinity potential of his nonpersonal self as Paradise. … Thus did the Father project reality in two actual phases—the personal and the nonpersonal, the spiritual and the nonspiritual.

Paradise is not ancestral to any being or living entity; it is not a creator. Personality and mind-spirit relationships are transmissible, but pattern is not. Patterns are never reflections; they are duplications—reproductions. Paradise is the absolute of patterns; Havona is an exhibit of these potentials in actuality.

ch06.s3.u1.k: All physical force, energy, and matter are one, proceeding from nether Paradise and returning there.
ch06.s3.u1.p: No personalities sojourn on nether Paradise, and it has nothing to do with the affairs of spirit intelligences; it is the realm of physical reality. The text says that all force, energy, and matter are one and that, after completing its space circuit, it finally returns to its source. Even the world of stars and atoms belongs to a vast circuit that goes out from the Father's house and returns.

text: Concerning nether Paradise, we know only that which is revealed; personalities do not sojourn there. It has nothing whatever to do with the affairs of spirit intelligences, nor does the Deity Absolute there function.
All physical force, energy, and matter are one. All force-energy originally proceeded from nether Paradise and will eventually return thereto following the completion of its space circuit.

ch06.s3.u2.k: Gravity is the all-powerful grasp with which the physical presence of Paradise holds all worlds.
ch06.s3.u2.p: Stars, suns, and planets are strung on a single invisible strand, the gravity of Paradise. The text pictures gravity as the omnipotent strand of the universe's adornment and says that everything is drawn inward toward Paradise. Behind the gravity physics measures lies the presence of God drawing all things to himself. The universe does not scatter; it gathers toward its center.

text: The inescapable pull of gravity effectively grips all the worlds of all the universes of all space. Gravity is the all-powerful grasp of the physical presence of Paradise. Gravity is the omnipotent strand on which are strung the gleaming stars, blazing suns, and whirling spheres which constitute the universal physical adornment of the eternal God, who is all things, fills all things, and in whom all things consist.

Paradise is the absolute source and the eternal focal point of all energy-matter in the universe of universes. … The universal presence of the Unqualified Absolute seems to be equivalent to the concept of a potential infinity of gravity extension, an elastic tension of Paradise presence. This concept aids us in grasping the fact that everything is drawn inward towards Paradise.

ch06.s3.u3.k: Space is a bestowal of Paradise, and the more spiritual a mind becomes, the less it responds to material gravity.
ch06.s3.u3.p: Even space is not empty nothingness but a gift bestowed by Paradise. Within it beings feel two kinds of pull: physical gravity measures quantity of energy, spiritual gravity measures quality of divinity. As a person grows Godlike, he is loosed from the weight of matter and grows more sensitive to the pull of spirit. The road to Paradise is also the road of laying down weight.

text: Space is neither a subabsolute condition within, nor the presence of, the Unqualified Absolute, neither is it a function of the Ultimate. It is a bestowal of Paradise, and the space of the grand universe and that of all outer regions is believed to be actually pervaded by the ancestral space potency of the Unqualified Absolute.

As the mind of any personality in the universe becomes more spiritual—Godlike—it becomes less responsive to material gravity. Reality, measured by physical-gravity response, is the antithesis of reality as determined by quality of spirit content. Physical-gravity action is a quantitative determiner of nonspirit energy; spiritual-gravity action is the qualitative measure of the living energy of divinity.

ch06.s4.u1.k: Paradise is the center of all creation, the origin of all personality, and the goal of desire for all spirit personalities.
ch06.s4.u1.p: All that has been, is, and will be comes forth from this central abode, so Paradise is both point of departure and point of arrival. Not all lower spirit beings of the local universes are bound directly for Paradise, yet for every supermaterial personality it remains the goal of desire. Longing for the source is a sense of direction written deep in every person.

text: Paradise is the universal headquarters of all personality activities and the source-center of all force-space and energy manifestations. Everything which has been, now is, or is yet to be, has come, now comes, or will come forth from this central abiding place of the eternal Gods. Paradise is the center of all creation, the source of all energies, and the place of primal origin of all personalities.

Paradise is unique in that it is the realm of primal origin and the final goal of destiny for all spirit personalities. Although it is true that not all of the lower spirit beings of the local universes are immediately destined to Paradise, Paradise still remains the goal of desire for all supermaterial personalities.

ch06.s4.u2.k: Every mortal who has chosen to do the Father's will has already embarked on the long Paradise trail.
ch06.s4.u2.p: In the end, the chief meaning of Paradise for man is that it is his real destiny. God's dwelling is the pattern of every universe headquarters and the real destiny of the immortal souls of ascending creatures. That journey does not begin in some distant future. It began the moment one resolved to do the Father's will.

text: God's residence is central and eternal, glorious and ideal. His home is the beauteous pattern for all universe headquarters worlds; and the central universe of his immediate indwelling is the pattern for all universes in their ideals, organization, and ultimate destiny.

After all, to mortals the most important thing about eternal Paradise is the fact that this perfect abode of the Universal Father is the real and far-distant destiny of the immortal souls of the mortal and material sons of God, the ascending creatures of the evolutionary worlds of time and space. Every God-knowing mortal who has espoused the career of doing the Father's will has already embarked upon the long, long Paradise trail of divinity pursuit and perfection attainment.

ch06.qs1: When I feel I have lost my way, what comfort is there in knowing that God is always found in the same place?
ch06.qs2: How does the teaching that the material world also comes from God change the way I treat my body and nature?
ch06.qs3: What can I do today to lay down some of the weight of matter and grow more responsive to the pull of spirit?
